analysis:
This batch has only documentation changes: a new changelog entry (changelog.d/coordinator-reconnect-stall.md, lines 1-4) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (date bump at line 3, drain paragraph at head 443-447, new handshake-deadline row at head ~1943). No executable source is supplied, so the claimed Swift behavior cannot be verified here.

Behavior described:
(1) A 30s coordinator handshake deadline (TCP/TLS/WebSocket upgrade) in CoordinatorConnectionHandshake.swift, followed by retry with the existing backoff. This is an availability improvement for TB-002 and relevant to T-057. It does not weaken TLS, since the timeout only cancels the attempt.
(2) stop/restart/start drain now completes without a coordinator acknowledgement only when there is no registered coordinator session and no unfinished requests; a registered session must still acknowledge before the deadline. The condition is narrow and does not change the reported docs for --force semantics.

The remaining question for integration is whether the 'no registered session' predicate in performLifecycleDrain (ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift) is race-free. A provider mid-reconnect could register after the check, and that could affect usage-settlement barrier guarantees and T-053 stale-authorization concerns, for example if the coordinator still holds a session or in-flight accounting. The supplied evidence neither shows nor refutes such a race. The source-level implementation and tests for the handshake timeout and the drain predicate were not in this batch, so I flag that as an unverified contract rather than a finding. The docs make no claims that alter the T-041 cache posture, attestation, or App Attest authorization.
